knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The 2022 Safe Work Australia guidance lists grinding, sanding, sawing and polishing among the processes that produce silica dust.
Respirable particles are generally not visible, so controls have to be in place before work starts, not after dust appears.
The NT WorkSafe guide says never to use compressed air, dry sweeping or general-purpose vacuum cleaners to clean surfaces or clothing.
The guidance ranks personal protective equipment as the least effective control and says workers should never rely solely on it.
Aggregate in terrazzo may contain silica, so the course treats terrazzo as silica-containing until its composition is known.

practicalCriteria: Lists each dust-generating task before the first pass
Names a control for each task before work starts
Stops when any listed control is missing
Does not use dry sweeping, compressed air or a general-purpose vacuum
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Task list showing each dust-generating process
Control chosen for each task, with a check record
stopWorkCriteria: Dry sweeping or compressed air used for clean-up
A missing control for any dust-generating task
